problem: Existing wayfinding aids for persons with visual impairments (PwVI) either only give navigation cues or need heavy environment instrumentation (beacons, RFID). General vision-language navigation agents assume users can give step-by-step instructions, and they are not built for PwVI.
motivation: PwVI need a guide that both physically leads them and exchanges semantic information about the environment by speech. Open-vocabulary vision-language grounding (CLIP) can replace special infrastructure and handle free-form, noisy speech commands. Closed-vocabulary detectors fail on synonyms and speech-recognition errors.
key_idea: A dialogue-driven guide robot that grounds free-form user language to saved landmark images with a fine-tuned CLIP, uses clarification dialogue to disambiguate goals, and navigates with a standard ROS stack while also describing the scene and answering VQA questions.
insight: Navigation succeeds whenever landmark recognition (LR) is correct (100% conditional success for both methods), so grounding quality is the bottleneck. The CLIP-vs-detector comparison shows this: 100% vs 46.67% LR and navigation success, with 2.4 vs 3.71 dialogue rounds. Open-vocabulary matching handles synonyms and mistranscriptions ('couch', 'coach'), and disambiguation dialogue adds attributes to the query. Confirm-before-go also makes wrong SR/NLU mostly harmless for navigation.
method: Audio interface: Whisper speech recognition for input and Google TTS for output via a wireless headset, connected through ROS.
NLU: DIET intent classifier and entity recognizer trained on 1092 self-collected sentences that include misspellings and phonetic variants, with multi-intent and unknown-intent handling.
Landmark mapping: during laser SLAM, one key press saves the robot pose and an RGB image of each landmark, with no labels.
Landmark recognition: CLIP ViT-B/32 fine-tuned on 544 image-text pairs (lr 8e-6, 35 epochs) picks the landmark image with the highest cosine similarity to the memorized goal description.
Disambiguation dialogue: asks for missing objects or attributes, merges them into the query, and confirms the goal before navigating.
Environment understanding: a Detic object detector with NMS, a confidence filter and top-3 classes produces descriptions, and a ViLT VQA model fine-tuned on 10252 triplets answers questions.
Navigation: ROS move_base with A* global and DWA local planners, AMCL localization, a physical T-handle, and user-adjustable speed, pause and resume.

setting.backbone: CLIP ViT-B/32 (fine-tuned) + DIET NLU (trained) + Whisper (frozen) + Detic detector + ViLT VQA (fine-tuned)
setting.training_data: Custom in-environment data: 1092 NLU sentences, 544 CLIP image-text pairs, 10252 VQA (image, question, answer) triplets, all collected by the authors
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB (RealSense D435i) + 2D lidar for SLAM/localization + speech
setting.action_space: Goal poses sent to ROS move_base (A*/DWA), non-negative velocity with user-adjustable maximum
setting.privileged: Pre-built SLAM map with manually saved landmark images and poses (pre-exploration)

numbers.eval_set_note: 5 blindfolded participants x 3 routes = 15 trials per method
numbers.extra: Pre-built map with saved landmarks; the baseline is a fine-tuned closed-vocabulary detector; real robot
numbers.evidence: Table 3 (success rates of LR and navigation): Ours 100 / 2.4 / 100 / 100

numbers_note: No standard benchmark; only a small real-world user study (N=5). Baseline detector: LR 46.67, rounds 3.71, navigation 46.67. Other module accuracies: SR 70.19, NLU 85.26, EnvDes full 45.45 / partial 75.76, VQA 82.43, NavAdj 100.
results: With CLIP, DRAGON reached 100% landmark-recognition and navigation success in 15 trials, versus 46.67% for a fine-tuned closed-vocabulary detector baseline, and needed fewer dialogue rounds (2.4 vs 3.71). Users preferred CLIP, with an overall experience score about 1.60 higher on average. NLU accuracy was 85.26%, and VQA accuracy 82.43%.
limitations: Pilot study with only 5 sighted, blindfolded university students, not actual PwVI, in one indoor environment.

Rule-based dialogue, mediocre speech recognition (70.19%), and limited RGB-only descriptions and VQA (EnvDes full-correct 45.45%); landmarks must be manually pre-mapped, and network delays slow responses.
